newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on weakening Japanese yen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on weakening Japanese yen.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Thursday lower as the yen's depreciation against the dollar sparked worries about the nation's economy, brokers said.

"The yen's fall will weaken price competitiveness of Korean products. This chilled investors' anticipation of an economic turnaround," said Kim Myung-jo of Hyundai Securities. South Korea and Japan compete with similar products in global market.
State-funded Korea Development Institute on Thursday lowered its forecast for 1997 gross domestic product growth to six percent from an earlier estimate of 6.4 percent.
The composite stock index fell 10.62 points to 688.04.
"Investors remain disappointed as the market has tried in vain to test the psychological 700 level," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.

Brokers said blue chip manufacturing shares led the index fall. Those stocks also faced consolidation after rallying on advanced buying ahead of an expansion in the foreign stock ownership ceiling on May 2.
Samsung Electronics shed 1,600 won to 62,900 and POSCO lost 2,000 won to 51,500.
Brokers said the market ignored the government's plan to allow more funds issuances for foreign investment in local stocks.
The finance ministry said domestic investment trust firms were allowed to issue beneficiary certificates for foreign investment in local stocks without limit until the end of June.
"I doubt how much foreign money will really flow in with the move," said Kim of Dongsuh.
Active institutional buying continued in selective small capitalised shares, but brokers said those shares would also face a consolidation.
"I expect the index to retreat to the 670 level on a consolidation and then to rebound," said Hyundai's Kim.
